use_cases.title: Automated matching of clean invoices with a daily exceptions list
use_cases.problem: Invoices are keyed into NetSuite manually and matched against PO and goods receipt; exceptions take about five days and are tracked in a single person's spreadsheet.

evidence.quote: Somebody opens each one, keys it into NetSuite, and then matches it against the purchase order and the goods receipt.
evidence.speaker: Dana Whitfield

evidence.quote: Aivar proposed starting with automated matching of clean invoices, and a daily exceptions list that replaces the spreadsheet.
evidence.speaker: Tom Becker

use_cases.customer_value: Clean invoices matched automatically and a short list of real exceptions for the team to look at.
use_cases.validation_question: What read/write access to NetSuite can be granted and how soon can the security review be requested?
use_cases.company_value: Anchor engagement for AP automation; reusable invoice matching pattern on AWS that can expand to onboarding.
current_process: Invoices arrive by email in the ap-invoices shared mailbox
Somebody opens each invoice and keys it into NetSuite
Invoice is matched against the purchase order and goods receipt
Exceptions are tracked in Raj's spreadsheet, updated by hand every morning
data_sources_and_apis: Supplier portal weekly CSV export (no API)
dependencies_and_blockers: Security review needed for direct write access to NetSuite, takes a few weeks to schedule
Supplier portal has no API; weekly CSV only
Marcus must decide whether the exceptions spreadsheet can be shared
stated_metrics: about two days for clean invoices
closer to five days for exceptions

use_cases.title: Read-only first integration that avoids the NetSuite write-access review
use_cases.problem: Write access to NetSuite needs a security review that takes a few weeks to schedule.

evidence.quote: Lena: confirm what read access to NetSuite can be granted without a full security review.
evidence.speaker: Tom Becker

evidence.quote: please tell us what access you will need as soon as you know.
evidence.speaker: Marcus Obi

use_cases.why_hidden: Nobody has said whether the solution can deliver value with read-only access, or how results would get back into NetSuite without a direct write.
use_cases.customer_value: Earlier value without waiting on the security review.
use_cases.company_value: De-risks the delivery start; a phased integration architecture.
use_cases.validation_question: Could matched results be posted to NetSuite by an AP user or through an existing import, rather than by direct tool write access?
dependencies_and_blockers: Security review for write access takes a few weeks to schedule

use_cases.title: Automated invoice capture from the ap-invoices shared mailbox
use_cases.problem: Automatic matching needs structured invoice data. Today every emailed invoice is opened and keyed into NetSuite by hand, so matching cannot be automatic unless intake and data extraction are automated first.

evidence.quote: most of those arrive by email into a shared mailbox, ap-invoices. Somebody opens each one, keys it into NetSuite
evidence.speaker: Dana Whitfield

evidence.quote: We are now closer to 5,200 invoices in a busy month, not 4,500
evidence.speaker: Marcus Obi

use_cases.why_hidden: The customers asked for automatic matching. Nobody asked to automate the mailbox intake or the extraction of invoice fields, which comes before matching.
use_cases.customer_value: Removes manual keying for a growing invoice volume handled by a three-person team.
use_cases.company_value: Adds a document ingestion and extraction workstream; a reusable intelligent document processing pattern on AWS.
use_cases.validation_question: In what formats do invoices arrive in ap-invoices (PDF, scanned image, email body), and do any invoices arrive outside the mailbox?
current_process: Invoices arrive by email into the ap-invoices shared mailbox
Somebody opens each one and keys it into NetSuite
dependencies_and_blockers: Write access to NetSuite requires a security review
stated_metrics: closer to 5,200 invoices in a busy month

use_cases.title: Daily exceptions list depends on a weekly-only supplier portal feed
use_cases.problem: Aivar proposed a daily exceptions list. The supplier portal only provides a weekly CSV export, so any matching that depends on portal data may be up to a week stale. A robust CSV ingestion pipeline is needed because the earlier RPA approach broke.

evidence.quote: The supplier portal is a separate vendor product and it has no API, so we only get data out of it as a weekly CSV export.
evidence.speaker: Lena Kowalski

evidence.quote: Aivar proposed starting with automated matching of clean invoices, and a daily exceptions list that replaces the spreadsheet.
evidence.speaker: Tom Becker

use_cases.why_hidden: Nobody pointed out that the daily cadence and the weekly feed conflict. It was also not said which matching data (for example goods receipts) comes from the portal.
use_cases.customer_value: Exceptions list that reflects the actual data freshness; no repeat of the RPA failure.
use_cases.company_value: Data ingestion pipeline workstream; sets realistic expectations early.
use_cases.validation_question: Which fields needed for matching come only from the portal CSV, and can the export be run more often than weekly?
current_process: Weekly CSV export from the supplier portal
dependencies_and_blockers: API request to portal vendor open for a year with no answer

use_cases.title: Exception baseline and root-cause analytics
use_cases.problem: Nobody has measured how many exceptions there are. The only view is a hand-updated spreadsheet of about 60 open items. Without a baseline, the success of the project cannot be shown and the causes of exceptions cannot be addressed.

evidence.quote: nobody has measured exactly how many there are.
evidence.speaker: Marcus Obi

evidence.quote: He tracks about 60 open exceptions at any time and updates it by hand every morning.
evidence.speaker: Tom Becker

use_cases.why_hidden: The customers asked for a short exceptions list. They did not ask for measurement, trends, or analysis of exception causes such as price differences or missing receipts.
use_cases.customer_value: Gives a baseline to prove improvement and targets the most common causes of exceptions.
use_cases.company_value: Adds an analytics and reporting layer; measurable success criteria for the engagement.
use_cases.validation_question: Would you want exception counts, ageing and causes reported per supplier and per month?
current_process: Raj updates the spreadsheet by hand every morning
dependencies_and_blockers: Marcus must agree before the spreadsheet is shared
stated_metrics: about 60 open exceptions at any time
closer to five days for exceptions

use_cases.title: Approval routing and audit trail
use_cases.problem: Approval history had to be rebuilt from emails for auditors, and approval thresholds differ by supplier category and are kept in a SharePoint document that is not always current.

evidence.quote: Our auditors asked about approvals last quarter, and honestly we had to rebuild the trail from emails.

evidence.quote: the current list lives in a SharePoint document that is not always up to date.

use_cases.customer_value: A clear record of who approved what.
use_cases.validation_question: Who are the approvers and what are the thresholds per supplier category?
use_cases.company_value: Extends scope to approval workflow and audit reporting.
current_process: Approvals happen and the trail is reconstructed from emails when auditors ask
dependencies_and_blockers: Threshold list is not always up to date

use_cases.title: Shared supplier master data linking onboarding and approval routing
use_cases.problem: Approval thresholds depend on supplier category, and the threshold list is out of date. Onboarding is where supplier categories would originate, and the same people are involved in both, so shared supplier master data would serve both processes.

evidence.quote: Dana confirmed that approval thresholds differ by supplier category, and that the current list lives in a SharePoint document that is not always up to date.
evidence.speaker: Tom Becker

evidence.quote: Some of the same people are involved.
evidence.speaker: Marcus Obi

use_cases.why_hidden: Onboarding was deferred as a separate topic. Nobody linked supplier category data to invoice routing.
use_cases.customer_value: Routing rules that stay current; less rework later in the onboarding phase.
use_cases.company_value: Natural bridge into the onboarding follow-on engagement.
use_cases.validation_question: Where is a supplier's category recorded today, and who sets it during onboarding?
dependencies_and_blockers: Threshold list is not always up to date

use_cases.title: Replace email as the de facto exception and approval workflow
use_cases.problem: Email is used to chase people when Raj is away and is the only source for rebuilding the approval trail. Email is acting as the workflow and record system.

evidence.quote: We chase people by email until he is back. It has happened a couple of times.

evidence.quote: Our auditors asked about approvals last quarter, and honestly we had to rebuild the trail from emails.

use_cases.why_hidden: Nobody asked for automated notifications, assignment or escalation of exceptions.
use_cases.customer_value: Removes the dependency on one person; exceptions are routed and escalated automatically.
use_cases.company_value: Workflow and notification scope; a reusable case-management pattern.
use_cases.validation_question: Who needs to act on an exception (suppliers, requesters, approvers), and how are they contacted today?
current_process: People are chased by email when Raj is out

use_cases.title: Capacity pressure from supplier growth
use_cases.problem: Invoice volume rose because new suppliers were onboarded, while the team stays at three people. Each new supplier adds load, so the solution must scale and onboarding speed affects AP volume.

evidence.quote: two new suppliers came on in September.
evidence.speaker: Marcus Obi

evidence.quote: Our accounts payable team is three people, and we process about 4,500 invoices a month.
evidence.speaker: Marcus Obi

use_cases.why_hidden: No growth forecast or capacity target was stated.
use_cases.company_value: Justifies a scalable serverless design and an onboarding follow-on.
use_cases.validation_question: How many new suppliers do you expect over the next year?

use_cases.title: Supplier onboarding (later phase)
use_cases.problem: Supplier onboarding takes far too long.

evidence.quote: supplier onboarding is taking us far too long, and if the invoice work goes well I would like to look at it next.
evidence.speaker: Marcus Obi

use_cases.validation_question: What does the current onboarding process look like and who is involved?
use_cases.company_value: Potential follow-on engagement after invoice matching.
dependencies_and_blockers: Customers asked to not mix it in yet; invoice matching first

use_cases.title: Finance data access governance for the new solution
use_cases.problem: Raj is reluctant to share exception data outside finance. This implies the new solution will need role-based access and data handling rules for finance data.

evidence.quote: Raj said he is not comfortable sharing the spreadsheet outside the finance team until Marcus agrees.
evidence.speaker: Tom Becker

use_cases.why_hidden: Nobody discussed access controls or data classification for the future system.
use_cases.customer_value: Finance data is visible only to authorised staff.
use_cases.validation_question: Who outside finance may see exception and invoice data in the new tool?
